description:
Hiking distance: 3 km.

Elevation gain: 360m

The Silent Pass Trail is a short, moderately steep trail with panoramic views from a lake and meadow. It is a fairly easy hike, suitable for family day-hikes. The trail also serves as a mountaineering access to the Spillimacheen Glacier.

The trail travels through mature forest as it crosses over several small creeks and wet areas before entering an avalanche path. Hike up this slide area and continue ascending through sub-alpine meadows until you reach Silent Lake.

The trail is not maintained beyond this point but hiking through the open terrain is rewarded by views of the peaks of Glacier National Park to the northwest and Spillimacheen Glacier to the southeast.

Silent Pass is a very popular snowmobiling destination in snow season. The trail is maintained in partnership with Golden Snowmobile Club. There is a mobile warming shelter for emergency. A fee for the groomed trail along lower elevation roads is charged. Trail report and info: https://sledgolden.com/
directions:
From the small community of Parson, drive west along the main Spillimacheen Road and North Fork Road until reaching the 46 km junction. Turn onto the McMurdo Creek Road, follow the main haul road, and park in the vicinity of km 58.5. Low clearance vehicles may have to park just before km 57.

Winter trailhead varies depending on where trail grooming starts. This is an active radio controlled industrial haul road. USE CAUTION AND A RADIO.
title: Silent Pass Trail
